topIssues.title: op-supernode: Superroot SLA Updates
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
The SLA of the Superroot object is ill-defined, but also it is not currently behaving as we'd like.

The addage from Proofs is "whenever you can get output roots for all the chains, you should be able to provide a super root"

What this means to me is that we should ensure two distinct categories:

1: the superroot should be eagerly available. That is, if there are output roots at the timestamp for all chains, let's construct the super-root

2: the extended information regarding verification and local derivation must accurately represent the condition of data which yielded the superroot. IE - if the root is built from un-verified components, that should be obvious when inspecting the verification and local safety information.


DoD: Super-Root API is fully integrated with Proofs testing.
Probably a co-task between @axelKingsley and @Inphi

topIssues.title: op-chain-ops: update check super root script to work with super node
topIssues.author: stevennevins
topIssues.body:
The verification script that we have used previously to verify that a SuperRoot was valid needs to be updated to work with SuperNode 

We need to update the inputs to use a SuperNode RPC for the dependency set.

And remove the need to pass each chain RPC for the dependency set.


Old API

```
go run op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root/main.go --rpc-endpoints $RPC_URL_1,$RPC_URL_2 --timestamp $SUPER_ROOT_TIMESTAMP
go run op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root/main.go --rpc-endpoints $RPC_URL_1,$RPC_URL_2
```

New API

```
go run op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root/main.go --super-node-rpc $SUPER_NODE_RPC --timestamp $SUPER_ROOT_TIMESTAMP
go run op-chain-ops/cmd/check-super-root/main.go --super-node-rpc $SUPER_NODE_RPC
```

topPRs.title: op-supernode: test same timestamp interop
topPRs.author: axelKingsley
topPRs.body:
# Tool Use Notice

Entirely generated Acceptance Tests. I read over the log output and saw that the correct conditions were being exercised, but still need to do my own self-review. Will be marked for full review after self-review.

# Same Timestamp Tests

Presently, the expected behavior is that no same-timestamp interop will work.

These tests demonstrate that same-timestamp Executing Messages are currently rejected.

As same-timestamp inclusion is implemented:

- Simple test will begin to fail because a same-timestamp EM gets included. B will no longer experience replacement.

- Transitive-Invalid test will continue to pass because the invalid EM at the same timestamp causes the whole chain of dependencies to become invalid, and so both chains still see a replacement.

topPRs.title: op-devstack: parallelize service startup and batch migration transactions
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Problem Statement

Devstack network setup is slow because all services start sequentially and the superroot migration issues ownership-transfer transactions one at a time, each waiting for an L1 block (~6s). This makes acceptance test iteration painfully slow.

## Solution

Add an `InParallel` option combinator that runs `AfterDeploy` phases concurrently, and refactor all devstack presets to group independent services by dependency level. Also batch ownership-transfer transactions in the superroot migration to reduce L1 block waits. 

Key changes:
- Add ParallelOption type and InParallel constructor to stack package
- Refactor system presets to use dependency-level parallelism (e.g. L2 CL + Faucets in parallel, then Batcher + Proposer in parallel)
- Add SendTxs batch utility to transactions package
- Parallelize L2 safe head polling across chains in superroot migration
- Batch pre-migration and post-migration ownership transfers
- Deduplicate shared proxy admin addresses in batched transfers

## Testing

On my machine, proofs and the minimal interop presets are setup in half the time.

topPRs.title: op-devstack: Reduce time for superroot migration
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Batch ownership-transfer transactions in the superroot migration to reduce L1 block waits.
Doing so shaves off a minute or two waiting for the superroot devstack migration.

topPRs.title: test(contracts): improve DelayedWETH test coverage with fuzz tests
topPRs.author: devin-ai-integration
topPRs.body:
# test(contracts): convert DelayedWETH tests to fuzz and add coverage

## Summary

Enhances `DelayedWETH.t.sol` by converting 12 focused tests to fuzz tests and adding 2 new tests for previously uncovered code paths.

**Fuzz conversions (12 tests):**
- `unlock`: fuzz sub-account address and amounts; fuzz double-unlock with variable amounts and time deltas
- `withdraw` (both 1-arg and 2-arg overloads): fuzz deposit/withdraw amounts, fuzz time-before-delay, fuzz over-withdrawal amounts
- `hold`: fuzz hold amounts for both overloads; fuzz non-owner address for access control
- `recover`: fuzz non-owner address for access control

**New coverage (2 tests):**
- `testFuzz_recover_partialAmount_succeeds` — covers the `_wad < address(this).balance` branch in `recover()`, which was previously untested (only full-balance and over-balance recovery had coverage)
- `test_version_validFormat_succeeds` — validates `version()` returns a parseable semver string via `SemverComp.parse()`

No tests were removed. Tests that target specific scenarios (paused, locked with timestamp=0) were left as focused tests.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Fuzz bounds correctness**: Verify `bound()` ranges won't cause overflow or vacuous passes — particularly `_wad1 + _wad2` (both `uint128.max`), `_deposit + _extra` (both `uint192.max`), and `_timeBefore` bounded to `delayedWeth.delay()` (assumes delay > 0)
- [ ] **`vm.deal` replacing balance**: Fuzzed withdraw/hold tests use `vm.deal(alice, _wad)` which *sets* alice's ETH balance rather than relying on the pre-existing 10000 ether from setUp — confirm this doesn't mask any edge case the originals caught
- [ ] **Partial recovery test**: `testFuzz_recover_partialAmount_succeeds` bounds `_wad` to `[0, _balance - 1)` — verify this correctly exercises the `amount = _wad` path (not `amount = address(this).balance`)
- [ ] Run `just test-dev --match-path test/dispute/DelayedWETH.t.sol -v` with higher fuzz runs (`FOUNDRY_FUZZ_RUNS=1000`) to stress-test bounds

### Notes
- Requested by: @aliersh
- [Link to Devin run](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5e66bf3514e64a46a3b50f565a8bc9e8)
